findings.bible: Clear section: 'once one is bound, however, a requested depth/stencil aspect with no DSV is deliberately a legal no-op, matching D3D11' (renderer-level statement).
findings.target: modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp::GraphicsDevice::Clear(ClearOptions,...) throws System::InvalidOperationException('Cannot clear depth or stencil because the device does not have an active depth or stencil buffer') before any renderer call when the request names a missing plane. modules/renderers/directx11/src/DirectX11Renderer.cpp::ClearDepth guards on currentDSV_ and directx12/src/DirectX12Renderer.cpp::ClearImpl on boundDsv_.ptr, so the no-op exists only beneath the public route. xna4-decomp GraphicsDevice.Clear: when D3D9 Clear fails and DefaultClearOptions lacks the requested depth/stencil it throws InvalidOperationException(CannotClearNullDepth), i.e. real XNA 4.0 does NOT treat it as a legal no-op. The site's own deep-dives/graphics/graphicsdevice-contract.html#clear-masking says it throws 'as Microsoft XNA does'.
findings.site_now: direct3d-presentation-and-state.html#clears: 'A requested depth or stencil clear with no view bound is a legal no-op, as in XNA.' Contradicts graphicsdevice-contract#clear-masking and the XNA reference; the 'as in XNA' comes from a CNA source comment in DirectX12Renderer.cpp (ClearImpl) that the decompile refutes.

fix.old_html: A requested depth or stencil clear with no view bound is a legal no-op, as in XNA.
fix.html: Inside the renderer a depth or stencil clear with no view bound is a no-op (Direct3D 11 guards on its bound view, Direct3D 12 on boundDsv_), but the public GraphicsDevice::Clear never lets such a request through: it throws InvalidOperationException first, as XNA 4.0 does (see clear masking).

findings.target: modules/renderers/directx9/src/D3D9EffectDraw.cpp (ResolveD3D9TextureEXT / ResolveD3D9TextureCubeEXT comments): GpuDrawParams::texture0/texture1 are const ITextureRenderer*; a RenderTarget2D's renderer (D3D9RenderTargetRenderer) is an unrelated sibling of D3D9TextureRenderer, and the old unconditional static_cast handed a garbage IDirect3DTexture9* to SetTexture, crashing later on DXVK's async shader-compiler thread. Fixed by dynamic_cast resolution to either class (2D and cube). D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp has the same resolver (previously drew untextured). modules/renderers/directx9/examples/CMakeLists.txt registers DirectX9_RenderTarget_EffectSource, _ProducerConsumer and _SamplingOrientation.

fix.anchor: render-targets (append as the last <li> of the section's list)
fix.html: • Sampling a target as a texture. A RenderTarget2D or RenderTargetCube handed to a stock effect as its texture is a different concrete renderer class from an ordinary texture, and GpuDrawParams carries only the common ITextureRenderer pointer. The stock-effect dispatch used to static_cast that pointer to the plain-texture class, which passed a garbage IDirect3DTexture9* to SetTexture and crashed later on DXVK's shader-compiler thread, while SpriteBatch silently drew untextured. D3D9EffectDraw.cpp and D3D9SpriteBatch.cpp now resolve the native texture with a dynamic_cast to either class (ResolveD3D9TextureEXT, plus a cube counterpart). DirectX9_RenderTarget_EffectSource, DirectX9_RenderTarget_ProducerConsumer and DirectX9_RenderTarget_SamplingOrientation are registered for this renderer as cross-renderer controls.

fix.html: At this snapshot the DIRECTX12 family implements the device, a single command queue, four descriptor allocators, two frame slots with one shared fence, per-resource barrier tracking (D3D12ResourceStateTracker), root-signature and pipeline-state caches, a per-slot sampler system, buffers, 2D, cube and 3D textures, render targets with MRT, device-queried MSAA and mip generation, occlusion queries, the stock shader variants, SpriteBatch, run-time ShaderEffect HLSL and device-removed recovery; the sections below show where each part differs from the Direct3D 11 route.

findings.bible: Usage section: 'A redundant bind is not a no-op: native resolve/finalization can run before the resource is rebound, and a discard target receives its three-aspect clear again.' (ledger WP10-ch28-116 marked 'confirmed')
findings.target: modules/graphics/src/Xna/GraphicsDevice.cpp::GraphicsDevice::SetRenderTargets: 'SOFTWARE-222: Microsoft XNA returns immediately when the complete binding set is unchanged ... so repeated bindings do not resolve/discard content or reset application viewport/scissor state' - it compares each target resource and cube face and returns before validation, the renderer call, the DiscardContents clear or the viewport reset (only exception: boundRenderTargetDestroyed_). Pinned by modules/graphics/tests/.../RenderTargetSemanticsTests.cpp; docs/software-easygl-parity-ledger.md records 'identical binding sets are true no-ops'; plans/plan_directx12_parity.md DX12-0023 describes the early return. The ledger's own WP11-ch30-022 records this same TARGET fact as a correction.
findings.site_now: direct3d11-and-12-resources.html#usage says 'A redundant bind is not a no-op: finalisation of the outgoing binding runs first, and a discard target is cleared again.' This contradicts render-targets-clears-and-viewports.html#rebinding ('Rebinding the same set is a no-op ... descriptions that say ... rebinding a DiscardContents target clears it again ... describe an older revision'), graphicsdevice-contract.html and sdl-renderer-2d-contract.html#clears-targets.

fix.old_html: A redundant bind is not a no-op: finalisation of the outgoing binding runs first, and a discard target is cleared again.
fix.html: Rebinding an identical target set does nothing: GraphicsDevice::SetRenderTargets returns early when every target and cube face matches the current binding, as XNA does (rebinding is a no-op), before any resolve, discard clear or viewport reset. A genuine change of binding, including a different cube face, finalises the outgoing binding first and clears a DiscardContents target again.

findings.target: modules/renderers/sdl-renderer/examples/sdlrenderer_texture_address_mode_clamp_test.cpp: SampleAtUOnePointTwoFive reads x = W*5/8 of a 4-texel source rectangle on a 2-texel texture, i.e. U = 1.25 texture widths = texel coordinate 2.5. In texel units 1.25 lies inside texel 1, where Clamp and Wrap both give blue, so the case would not discriminate.
findings.site_now: sdl-renderer-2d-contract.html#address-modes says 'source position 1.25' and 'source position 1.25 of the oversized range' without a unit; a reader who takes the source rectangle's texel units (0 to 4) reads the wrong texel and cannot reproduce 'Wrap gives red'.

fix.old_html: // read the pixel at x = W * 5 / 8: source position 1.25 of the oversized range
fix.html:
// read the pixel at x = W * 5 / 8: U = 1.25 texture widths (texel 2.5 of the 4-texel source rectangle),
// one texel past the 2-texel texture: Clamp gives texel 1 (blue), Wrap gives texel 0 (red)

findings.bible: Animated sprite-sheet: 'a fixed per-Update() frame-index increment instead of elapsed-time-based timing, so the outcome never depends on wall-clock frame speed'.
findings.target: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp::Game::Tick: with IsFixedTimeStep (the default, and not changed by sdlrenderer_sample_animated_spritesheet_test.cpp) a tick runs 'while accumulatedElapsedTime_ >= TargetElapsedTime_ { Update }', so a slow frame runs several Update calls before one Draw. The fixture's check fires on the first Draw with updatesRun_ >= 3 and expects frameCounter_ % 2 == 1, so a catch-up burst that makes it 4 flips the frame.
findings.site_now: sdl-renderer-2d-contract.html#readback: 'each Update() advances a counter instead of using elapsed time, so the outcome never depends on frame timing'.

fix.old_html: so the outcome never depends on frame timing;
fix.html: so the animation does not depend on elapsed time (it still assumes one Update() per Draw() before the check: the fixed-timestep loop can run several updates in one tick on a slow frame);

findings.bible: LZX section: 'The strongest decoder oracle is cross-implementation ... That oracle found a real heap-buffer-overflow in the long-code table-growth path, a class of defect that self-consistency fixtures could miss.' (ledger WP12-ch34-017 HISTORICAL ONLY: 'no TARGET record names it')
findings.target: modules/content/src/Xnb/LzxDecoder.cpp::LzxDecoder::MakeDecodeTable carries explicit guards ('plans/plan_xnb.md XNB-30A hardening: FNA's own C# port relies on the CLR's automatic bounds-checked array access here ... a direct std::vector::operator[] port has no equivalent safety net ... found by the XNB-30A fuzz test': leaf >= table.size() and (next_symbol << 1) + 1 >= table.size() return 1), and two match_offset range checks (XNB-30 hardening) in the aligned/verbatim block paths. plans/plan_xnb.md rows XNB-30 and XNB-30A record it: the deterministic mutation fuzzer LzxDecoderFuzzTests.cpp (2000 mutated inputs) found and fixed a real heap-buffer-overflow in MakeDecodeTable()'s long-code table-growth path, re-verified under -DCNA_SANITIZE=address,undefined; the Mono differential test (LzxDecoderDifferentialTests.cpp) supplies byte-exactness, not that finding. So a TARGET record exists, and the Bible credited the wrong tool.
findings.site_now: absent: xnb-container-and-object-graph.html#lzx calls the decoder a 'line-by-line C++ port ... keeping FNA's variable names, control flow and return codes' and names the oracle and the fuzzer, but says nothing about the guards where the port deliberately differs (safety added where C# relied on CLR array checks) or the defect they closed; content-robustness.html#oracles is silent as well.

fix.html: The port is line by line in control flow but not in memory safety. FNA's C# indexes its Huffman tables and window through CLR bounds-checked arrays, so a corrupt code-length table or match offset is a catchable exception there and undefined behaviour in a direct C++ port. LzxDecoder.cpp therefore rejects such input explicitly: MakeDecodeTable returns its error code when the long-code table-growth path would leave the table, and both match paths refuse an offset outside the window. The table-growth case was a real heap-buffer-overflow, found by the mutation fuzzer (not by the Mono comparison) and re-verified under AddressSanitizer and UBSan (plans/plan_xnb.md XNB-30 and XNB-30A). Keep those guards when comparing the port with the C# original.
